children: , the global banking and payments giant, fell 1.1% to approximately $136.66 around midday Friday after its economists shoved the first expected Federal Reserve rate cut deep into 2027. Citi now expects easing to begin in June, followed by three quarter-point cuts during the year. The message is blunt: expensive money could stick around much longer than investors hoped.

Citi is hardly limping into that environment. Its second-quarter results showed revenue exploding 14% to $24.8 billion and net income rocketing 45% to $5.8 billion. Net interest income climbed 13%, giving the bank a powerful earnings tailwind. But the bill is rising too. Expenses increased 5%, while net credit losses reached $2.4 billion.

Here is the catch: Citi now trades roughly 35.5% above its $100.89 tangible book value per share. The bargain-bin turnaround story is dead. Higher rates can keep lending spreads juicy, but they can also crack weaker borrowers and force banks to pay more for deposits. Citi must turn this rate windfall into durable earnings growthbecause investors are already paying for the comeback.

title: Citigroup Falls 1.1% as Its Rate-Cut Clock Jumps to 2027
